title: GRANT
description: Learn how to grant permissions on database objects to users using the GRANT statement.

data.text: The GRANT statement allows you to grant permissions on a securable (like a table) to a principal (like a user). Without permissions, users cannot interact with database objects.

data.title: GRANT Syntax
data.content: Grants permissions on a securable to a principal.
data.code:
GRANT permissions
ON securable TO principal;

items: Specify one or more permissions after the GRANT keywords (use commas for multiple permissions).
Specify a securable after the ON keyword (e.g., a table).
Specify the principal after the TO keyword (e.g., a user).

data.text: The following example demonstrates granting SELECT, INSERT, and DELETE permissions on a People table to a user named peter.

data.title: Setup and Grant Permissions
data.content: Creates HR database, People table, login, user, and grants SELECT permission.

data.text: After granting SELECT, user peter can query the People table but cannot insert or delete data.

data.title: Grant INSERT and DELETE
data.content: Grants additional INSERT and DELETE permissions to peter.
data.code:
GRANT INSERT, DELETE
ON People TO peter;

data.title: GRANT Key Points
points: Use GRANT to give users permissions on database objects.
You can grant multiple permissions in a single statement.
A securable is the resource (e.g., a table).
A principal is the entity receiving the permission (e.g., a user).
Grant only the minimum permissions needed for each user.
